$comment: Cross-layer delta L0206-D002 (AI-003 raw ToolCall.arguments JavaScript value domain). Scenarios live in conformance/agent/raw-arguments/*.json, discriminated by a top-level `raw_arguments` key. For each case a runner builds ONE ToolCall whose arguments are the case's value (fixture input, decoded from the value grammar), then observes that value -- by value, never by identity -- at every certified boundary: the constructed ToolCall.arguments; an AssistantMessage holding the call appended to a fresh session log and replayed from it (decode of the logged event); the tools/execution-start payload; the tools/pre-execute listener; execute; and, the tool reporting exactly one partial result through its update callback, the tools/update payload and the on-execution-update delivery (tool_execution_end carries no arguments: N/A), for a tool WITHOUT prepare_arguments whose schema is {type: object, properties: {}}. Every boundary must observe exactly `arguments`. The runner performs no decoding, normalization or conversion on the pipeline's behalf. VALUE GRAMMAR: {"utf16": units} is a string (units = UTF-16 code units 0..65535, so unpaired surrogates survive the file); {"number": token} is a number (see $defs.token: a named +Infinity/-Infinity/-0, or a canonical finite literal -- the PREFLIGHT there); {"$keys": [[units, value], ...]} is an object whose keys need code units; any other object is an object with those (ASCII) keys; an array is an array; true/false/null are themselves. OBJECTS COMPARE AS KEY SETS: enumeration order is L0206-D001's (K1), not this shape's. `provider_text` is the provider's argument text pinned Pi decoded (evidence only: Minion has no certified raw decoder; a future decoder must produce `arguments` from it).

token.$comment: L0206-D002-R002: a NAMED token (+Infinity, -Infinity, -0) or a FINITE LITERAL. NaN is not in the raw domain (JSON.parse cannot produce it). PREFLIGHT (language-neutral, before dispatch; a violation fails the document, never defaulted): a finite literal must denote a finite binary64 value AND be exactly that value's ECMAScript Number::toString -- so it names one binary64 value with no rounding or widening left to a binding (9007199254740993 and 1e999 are refused; write 9007199254740992 and +Infinity). An integral finite literal is the binding's integer representation of that exact value.
